title: Blood basophil percentage does not establish incremental prediction of exhaled nitric oxide beyond eosinophils: a two-cycle adult NHANES test
abstract: Adding a blood-basophil-percentage spline to eosinophils and conventional covariates did not establish improved log-FeNO prediction. After fitting NHANES2007–2008 adults (n=4036), target NHANES2009–2010 adults (n=4658) had baseline-minus-augmented weighted MSE gain -0.00052030 (95% source/target PSU-refit interval -0.00786073 to 0.00137459). Both source cross-validation and target point estimates favored the baseline. This is a model-specific negative result, not evidence that basophils lack physiological relevance or proof of equivalence.
